top.line: A blueprint for products with no server and no database of yours, with an MVP in a vault.
top.para: Phase one is a folder of HTML, CSS and JavaScript that runs offline and anywhere. The user brings the AI key, the storage and the passkey, so no request passes through you. Then the provider gaps, how to build and charge, a checklist for agents, and an MVP in a vault with a business plan.

in-short.line: Nine points: the architecture, the gaps, the team, the price, the checklist, the MVP.
in-short.para: No server or database of yours; native components, vendored, running anywhere; the user's key, storage and passkey; not in the line; the pieces mostly exist; build with agents and an explorer; charge for build, users and keys; a checklist for agents; an MVP and plan in a vault.

what.line: The pieces in one place, for founders and their agents, and a name.
what.para: Many earlier articles are one idea in pieces: passkeys, your own key, less code, Cloudflare blocks, explorer coding, your own newsroom, pay after the value. This is the blueprint, written for founders and for the agents that work with them. Its name: a no-server product, as distinct from serverless.

principles.line: Ten principles, from no server to charging for value.
principles.para: No server or database of yours; native web components; vendored libraries; offline and anywhere; the user brings the compute; the user's data stays with the user; the passkey is the identity; you are not in the line; version control and agents; charge for value, not servers.

example.line: An infographic studio, end to end, with nothing through the company.
example.para: The user opens static files, signs in with a passkey, connects OpenRouter by OAuth so requests bill their own credit, generates in the browser and keeps the results in their storage or Drive app folder. A simulation mode lets every feature work without a key.

gaps.line: Where the providers fall short today, and the opportunity.
gaps.para: No documented cap on a user-granted key; OpenAI and Google warn against developer keys in client code; Sign in with ChatGPT is a limited trial needing a backend; no provider checked pays the app that brings a customer; GitHub Pages is not for commercial SaaS, so move hosts to sell.

stack.para: Static files with native components; GitHub Pages to build, another static host to sell, or the folder shipped; a passkey with PRF; browser storage, an encrypted vault or the user's Drive; the user's capped key; payment by the provider, or a link with credit kept by the user.

build.line: Agents, a dev and a main site, synthetic users, and an explorer first.
build.para: An agent session maintains the repository, with a dev site for changes and a main site for customers. Synthetic users test every release. The team is hired as explorers, villagers, then town planners, and the first hire is an explorer working with the agents.

model.line: Charge for value: the build, the users, the keys, the installation.
model.para: Costs are almost nothing, so price is about value: a project to build a customer's site, a price per user, a share or fee for the keys even when users bring their own, and a licence for running it inside a customer's network.

mvp.line: The infographic studio, built and published in a vault.
mvp.para: One HTML file of seven web components, no framework and no server. Mostly simulated: a deterministic extractor stands in for the model. Inside the vault, the host holds the AI key, caps it and asks first, so the studio never sees it. Three synthetic users walked it before it was published.

business.line: Three businesses for somebody to build, with the plan in the vault.
business.para: The studio for one segment; a studio that builds no-server products for others; and the credit layer providers are missing, capped user keys and a share paid to the app. The vault's plan has customers, prices as hypotheses, go-to-market, ninety days, a calculator, risks and open questions.

next.line: Twelve steps an agent can mark done.
next.para: From one repository with dev and main, through no backend, web components, vendoring, offline and portable hosting, passkey sign-in, storage, the user's key and a simulation mode, to synthetic users and a payment path with no server of yours.

limits.line: Phase one, a proposed name, terms that change, products that do not fit, a simulated MVP.
limits.para: Some products will need a server later. The name is a proposal. Provider terms are as of 20 October 2026. Shared state between users needs more. The MVP is mostly simulated, and its own-key path has not yet run against a live key.

sources.line: A voice memo, provider documentation, coding.sgit.ai, nfrs.sgit.ai and earlier articles.
sources.para: A voice memo of 20 October 2026; provider documentation checked that day; coding.sgit.ai for components and nfrs.sgit.ai for the non-functional requirements; earlier articles on passkeys, your own key, less code, Cloudflare, explorer coding, your own newsroom, paying after the value and the vault across profiles; and Wardley on pioneers, settlers and town planners.
